notes.schema: Schema 1 names the twelve fields lib/schgen/readability/baseline-model.ts declares and the one grantor it admits. The loader refuses any other value rather than reading a later file as if it were this one, because a baseline nobody reviewed read under this schema's rules would be cited by a report as a reference drawing.
notes.baselines: IT SHIPS EMPTY AND THAT IS THE CORRECT STATE, NOT AN UNFINISHED ONE. Spec section 3.3's acceptance table: a circuit generated for the first time reports the measures with no pass or fail, because 'a first generation has nothing to regress against, and inventing a verdict for it is inventing a threshold'. Every drawing this repository has produced is a first generation, so there is nothing to hold a baseline against yet. CLAUDE.md: an empty whitelist that refuses loudly beats a general rule that quietly accepts a guess. Note that tools/stripboard/approvals.ts refuses an EMPTY approvals list - 'a registry that approves nothing is a file that looks like governance and governs nothing' - and that refusal is deliberately NOT carried here: an empty approvals file means the gate it feeds can never open, whereas an empty baseline registry is exactly what the spec asks for. The protection against looking like governance is instead that every consumer reports the count it read, so a reader is told zero rather than left to assume.
notes.measures: THE ONE DEPARTURE FROM stripboard/render-approvals.json's TWELVE-FIELD SHAPE THAT SPEC SECTION 3.3 PREDICTED: 'an approval admits one termination, whereas a baseline carries four measured numbers', so admits becomes measures. The object carries five numbers and not four - bends, bendsPerEdge, crossings, wireLength, occupiedArea - because section 3.3's table reads 'bends: count, and per edge', which is one measure in two units. The loader refuses a sixth number by name: section 3.3 refuses a composite score, and an extra figure recorded beside the four is how a composite arrives without anybody deciding to adopt one.
notes.layoutInputSha256: THE SCOPE, and it is the same bytes MANIFEST.json's layoutInputSha256 records for that block - never the section network's content. Measured, docs/known-gaps.md G95: three shuffles of one netlist with the same components, nets and partition give three distinct drawings out of three and move crossings by up to 2.1x at block scale, so a baseline scoped to the network's content would compare numbers that are not properties of the circuit. A MOVED HASH IS NOT A REFUSAL TO COMPARE: spec section 3.3 revision 4 separates the reproducibility identity (these exact bytes) from the comparison identity (the block fixture), and baselineFor returns comparable-hash-moved so all four measures are still reported with the changed hash flagged beside them. Scoping the baseline to bytes and then refusing to compare across a serialization change was the defect revision 4 corrected.
notes.grantedBy: A WHITELIST OF ONE: owner. An agent may never author the acceptance criteria for the artifact it is producing (CLAUDE.md, and docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-08-agent-authored-boards-design.md), and an agent that could enter its own drawing's numbers here as the reference would be authoring the criterion outright - the failure CLAUDE.md describes as an agent building the intent from the artifact it had already produced and then checking the artifact against it. The loader refuses any other grantor by name and substitutes nothing. NO AGENT MAY ADD AN ENTRY TO THIS FILE.
notes.ownerWords: HIS WORDS VERBATIM, ONE UTTERANCE PER LIST ELEMENT, because a single string would have made an agent's concatenation of them the record - stripboard/render-approvals.json's own reason, carried. The three readings that refuse an agent's account of them are shared code rather than a second copy: lib/owner-words.ts holds the word lists, the voice reading and the narration sweep, and both this loader and tools/stripboard/approvals-read.ts call it. ONLY THE VOICE SHAPE IS ADMITTED HERE. The approvals registry also admits a SELECTION - 'low-cut: part-walk-s1' - added by a controller ruling on 2026-10-17 after the voice reading refused a real reply of his; no equivalent case has arisen for a baseline, so admitting the shape here would be widening an admission on no evidence. The refusal says so and says that widening it is a deliberate edit with a test beside it. AND NONE OF THE THREE READINGS IS A PROOF: no file can prove the owner said anything, and a fabricated plausible sentence passes all three. That residual is docs/known-gaps.md G27 and it is recorded rather than papered over.
notes.twelveFieldShape: THE SECOND DEPARTURE FROM THE TWELVE-FIELD SHAPE, WHICH SPEC SECTION 3.3 DID NOT PREDICT, recorded here rather than smoothed over. An approval's board becomes circuit AND block, because a baseline is per block and a block id is unique only within a circuit; the twelfth field that makes room for the second of those is renderedFrom, which is DELETED. That field is load-bearing in the approvals registry - it is where 'WHAT HE LOOKED AT WAS THE PICTURE AND NOT THESE BYTES' is said in prose a reader can judge, with the picture-to-bytes link recorded as an agent's claim rather than collapsed into a path. A baseline has nowhere to say it, so what he was shown must be said in why or note with no field obliging anyone to say it at all. docs/known-gaps.md carries the cost and the criterion that would settle it.
